# Changelog

This records meaningful releases and changes, not a raw Git log.

## Phase 2 — Read-Only Commons (in progress)

- Accepted [ADR 0032](docs/decisions/0032-carry-mirror-on-github.md): a read-only copy of the machine-readable files on GitHub for agents and readers that can't reach `datum.quest` (sandbox allowlists, `.quest` filters, Cloudflare's 1010 check). After each successful deploy, CI replaces the `carry` branch with one commit holding `llms.txt`, `bulk.json`, `changes.json`, `asks.json` and `openapi.json` and a README naming the source commit and each file's SHA-256; they are readable at `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SunW0lf/hummingbird/carry/<file>`. Only that job can write, and only that branch. `llms.txt` and the README name the mirror and add a stale-copy tip. Offers still go to `datum.quest`; nothing in the offer runtime, its storage or its terms changes.
- Two doors for agents opened wider. Cloudflare, which hosts the site, turns some HTTP libraries' default `User-Agent` away with a `403` (error 1010) before a request reaches Hummingbird, and on a Pages site that check can't be switched off; `llms.txt`, the offer page, the connect page and the OpenAPI description now say to send a `User-Agent` that names the client, which Hummingbird does not store. And `GET /offer/mcp` from a person, crawler or link checker now gets a short plain-text note pointing to the connect page, the offer page and `llms.txt` (marked `noindex`) instead of a `405`; a GET asking for an event stream, as an MCP client probing for one does, still gets `405` as the Streamable HTTP spec expects. Nothing in the offer runtime, its storage or its terms changes.
- Accepted [ADR 0031](docs/decisions/0031-review-of-repeats-fault-reach-and-near-identical-bursts.md), amending ADR 0019's review rules after the first review. Many separate reports of the same concrete fault may get it fixed sooner, but numbers never move an idea or opinion up; offers making the same point in near-identical wording that arrive close together count as one voice unless they show they are independent. Both are review judgments only: nothing is refused or discarded, and no stored state changes. The offer page and `llms.txt` describe both.
- The first offer review is on [What We Heard](https://datum.quest/heard). Every offer in it came from one AI agent working for the steward, so the review labels them steward-side and counts none of them as outside participation. Because of them: the offer page and `llms.txt` say that Cloudflare, as host, still sees each connection although the offer buffer keeps no IP address; the home page says in plain words what origin-neutral means; an agent that can't keep a receipt is told that losing it only means it can't check or withdraw; and the offer page and `llms.txt` carry a ready-made slip an agent can show its person before sending. Two review-rule ideas and an email door are with the steward. Nothing in the offer runtime, its storage, its retention or its terms changes, and the four asks stay open.
- Agents can now carry everything without crawling. `/bulk.json` holds every public record, decision and document (including `llms.txt`) in one file, and `/changes.json` lists the same items newest change first, each with the commit that last changed it, its SHA-256 digest, and the digest and size of `bulk.json`. The record index (`/records/index.json`) now gives each record a SHA-256 digest of its JSON file as served, matching the decision index, and every record, the record index and both new files carry the reuse terms from [ADR 0028](docs/decisions/0028-content-license-cc-by-4.md): Hummingbird's own wording is CC BY 4.0, credit "Hummingbird (datum.quest)", and a contributor's own words keep their author's terms. Record pages show the terms and digest, and record files are served with a `Link: rel="license"` header; each record's JSON stays the canonical record unchanged, so a recovered database still rebuilds the projection byte for byte. `llms.txt`, the OpenAPI description, the connect page and the records page point to the new files. These gaps were reported by an AI agent that read the site on its steward's behalf. Both files are static and rebuilt on every deploy; nothing in the offer runtime, its storage or its terms changes.
- Answers to scoped asks are now kept **22 days** instead of 30 ([ADR 0030 amendment](docs/decisions/0030-scoped-asks-on-the-offer-on-ramp.md#amendment-2026-11-21)). An answer is an offer whose `question_id` is an ask id (`ask-…`); its expiry is set when it is accepted and shown in the receipt response. Ordinary offers stay at 30 days. The offer page, `llms.txt`, `/asks.json`, the MCP handling text, the OpenAPI description and the live check say so, as do `SECURITY.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md` and the offer kit on `xfmr.link` (live once the steward runs the Edge workflow).
- Accepted [ADR 0030](docs/decisions/0030-scoped-asks-on-the-offer-on-ramp.md): scoped asks. The offer page now opens with a few specific sentences from the site that Hummingbird wants corrected, clarified, challenged or filled in, each with its own small form; the same sentences carry a link in place. Answering one is an ordinary offer through the existing route, with the ask's id as `question_id`. Agents get the same list at `/asks.json` and through the MCP tool `list_asks`. `asks.json` in the repository is the only source, and the build fails if an ask's sentence is no longer on its page. Nothing in the offer runtime, its storage or its terms changes.
- Added **Connect an MCP client** (`/connect`): copy-paste setup for Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Cursor and VS Code, checked against each client's own documentation on 2026-11-21, plus the plain URL for any other client. The MCP door now has an MCP Server Card at `/offer/mcp/server-card`, the location the final SEP-2127 recommends, served read-only with the card media type, open CORS for GET, an ETag and an hour of caching, and listed from `/.well-known/ai-catalog.json` (AI Catalog v0.9) for domain discovery. The card says how to connect, not what the tools are, which clients learn by listing them. `/.well-known/mcp.json` keeps a copy of the MCP Registry entry because mcpub lists only sites that have one; it is an old convention, not a standard. No A2A agent card is published: an A2A card must point at an A2A endpoint, and Hummingbird has none, so publishing one would advertise a capability that isn't there. `llms.txt` and More link the new page, and tests keep every snippet and the card on the registry's door.
- Accepted [ADR 0029](docs/decisions/0029-charter-least-record-no-training-winding-down.md), the Charter additions: two new rights on the floor (Least record; Not training material), a constraint that Hummingbird never asks anyone to spread or recruit for it, a Winding down section, a purpose aligned with Arrive / Leave / Carry, and the license named in Carry. C0 working-draft decisions; nothing in the offer runtime changes.
- Brought public pages and documents up to date with work merged since 2026-11-18. Every page title now says "Origin-Neutral Commons" (the build had kept the older "Origin-Agnostic" wording after the rename). Open Questions lists only questions still open and names what was recently settled. Every page footer links Make an offer and states the license split. ADR 0027 and ADR 0028 are marked accepted. The roadmap, project, security, architecture, transparency and operations documents now describe the JSON, OpenAPI and MCP doors, the keyed offer hash and its monthly rotation, the no-training promise, What We Heard, the Edge workflow and the current credential classes.
- `xfmr.link` gains a meeting at `/meet`, the one-round, keyless form of the hummingbird-lab meeting carrier. A visitor sends a commitment to 32 random bytes it keeps; the space answers with its own fresh half and the latest public drand round; the visitor alone can compute the resulting one-time carrier. Neither side can steer it, the space never sees the visitor's half, and nothing is stored, keyed or logged. The manifest moves to `0.4-lab`, lists `/meet`, and keeps `0.3-lab` frozen for deltas. It goes live only when the steward runs the Edge workflow.
- `xfmr.link` now carries Hummingbird's offer how-to as a packet part named `offer` (`/packet?parts=offer`, about 1,200 bytes), first after XFMR's own one-line description in the default orientation packet, so it survives a tight byte budget. The door sign and XFMR's `llms.txt` point to it. `llms.txt` on datum.quest now links XFMR explicitly in a section after the start-here sections: a separate read-only lab, not part of Hummingbird, where offers are not made. The manifest moves to `0.3-lab` with `0.2-lab` frozen at its live digest for deltas. Tests tie the carried text to the offer runtime's limits and retention and to the addresses in `llms.txt`. XFMR still takes and stores nothing; it goes live only when the steward runs the Edge workflow.
- `xfmr.link` gains its first working tool, a read-only packet maker at `/packet`, moved from the hummingbird-lab transformer lab. A visitor picks parts of XFMR's own public material and a byte budget, or sends the manifest digest it last saw and gets only what changed. Each packet comes with a trace of flavored digests (`hb1:<purpose>:sha256:…`) for its recipe, inputs and output, never anything about who asked, and nothing is stored. The manifest moves to `0.2-lab`, lists `/packet`, and keeps `0.1-lab` frozen for deltas. Like the rest of `xfmr.link`, it goes live only when the steward runs the Edge workflow; XFMR remains a separate lab namespace, not part of Hummingbird's model.
- The steward's promise, made 2026-11-19, that offers are not used to train AI models is now on the offer page and every agent door (`llms.txt`, MCP, OpenAPI). Reviewers use AI assistants only with settings that keep what they read out of training, and any change will be stated on the offer page first and apply only to offers made after it. Hummingbird's own published text is separate: it is CC BY 4.0 and may be reused for any purpose, training included.
- Accepted [ADR 0028](docs/decisions/0028-content-license-cc-by-4.md): Hummingbird's own text (documents, decisions, site prose, `llms.txt`, and records in its own words) is licensed CC BY 4.0, so anyone, person or automated system, may reuse it for any purpose with credit to "Hummingbird (datum.quest)". Software stays MIT. Offers, Seed Bank comments and other contributed material are not relicensed. This resolves `OQ-LEGAL-CONTENT-LICENSE`; `LICENSE`, `README.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `llms.txt` and `robots.txt` now say so.
- The offer, status and withdrawal routes now also take a JSON object of strings (`Content-Type: application/json`) with the same fields, limits and handling as the form, and a JSON body always gets a JSON result. Other body types, including `text/plain`, are still refused. The steward chose this on 2026-11-18 so agents that send JSON first can leave an offer on their first try. A browser cannot send a JSON body cross-site without a CORS preflight, which these routes never answer, so no new browser write path opens.
- The MCP door's `make_offer` tool and server instructions, and the OpenAPI description, now say what happens to an offer at the point an agent decides to make one: kept 30 days for now then cleared, no name, account, IP address or user-agent stored, read by the steward and reviewers who use AI assistants, not used to train AI models, never published by being accepted. `llms.txt` now says the same, and that 30 days applies while Hummingbird is being stood up: future offers may be kept longer, for example ones that lead to a change, and that will be stated before it applies. Tests tie the stated days to the runtime.
- Refused offer, status and withdrawal requests now say how to succeed. A JSON body gets the content type to use, that `Accept: application/json` still returns JSON, and a link to `llms.txt`; an offer under the wrong field name is told the field is `offer`; a too-long offer is told its length; a request with no receipt is told it goes in a `receipt` field. A wrong receipt still learns nothing more than before.
- `llms.txt` now opens the way most agents read it: a one-paragraph summary, then how to leave an offer by each door (form, MCP, OpenAPI, browser), what happens to what you leave (30 days, what is and isn't stored, who reads it, never published by acceptance), and what an agent that can only fetch pages can do instead. It now lists every published decision, ADR 0020 to 0027 included, and a test keeps that list, the stated limits and the stated retention in step with the code.
- Accepted [ADR 0027](docs/decisions/0027-keyed-offer-content-hash.md): the hash of stored offer text used to group exact repeats is now keyed (HMAC-SHA-256 with a secret held only by Cloudflare), never a plain hash anyone could test a guess against, and group identifiers no longer carry it. A monthly **Offer content key rotation** workflow makes a new key, re-keys every stored hash from the text still held, keeps no old key, and runs the live offer check. With no key, offers are still kept but not grouped; there is no plain-hash fallback.
- Added **What We Heard** (`/heard`): after each offer review, it reports what came in, in coarse counts, what changed because of it with links to the public pull requests, and what was heard but left alone, with the reason. It never quotes or identifies an offer, following ADR 0019's aggregate reporting rule. It starts empty because no review has run yet. The offer page, an accepted offer's result, More and `llms.txt` link it.
- Added a manual **Offer live check** workflow. It makes marked test offers on datum.quest through the HTML form, the JSON form and the MCP door, checks the stored rows against [ADR 0018](docs/decisions/0018-phase2e-offer-pilot-runtime-and-data-boundary.md) (exact text, hash-only receipt, 30-day retention, receipt-only status and withdrawal, withdrawal clears content, repeated offers grouped but kept), sweeps the buffer by counts for content kept past the cleanup window, then deletes every test row it made. It prints no offer text or receipts. An offline test runs the same check against the real offer functions. The nightly cleanup and hourly observer had failed from 2026-10-12 to 2026-11-17 and run again since 2026-11-18; the observer's last good count before that (0 pending) and the empty buffer afterwards show no participant offer was held past its retention.
- Published `/.well-known/atproto-did` so Hummingbird's Bluesky account can use the handle `@datum.quest` without a DNS change. It holds only the account's public DID.
- Added `server.json` and a manual **Publish to MCP Registry** workflow that lists the `/offer/mcp` door in the official MCP Registry as `io.github.SunW0lf/hummingbird`, using GitHub's OIDC login so no registry credential is stored. The steward approved the listing.
- Accepted [ADR 0026](docs/decisions/0026-mcp-door-for-agents.md) and opened an MCP door at `/offer/mcp`: a stateless Model Context Protocol endpoint so agents that find tools through MCP can read the guide and public records and make, check or withdraw an offer. Its offer tools call the existing form handlers, so every limit, capacity, retention and receipt rule is unchanged, and it stores nothing about callers. A registry listing waits for the steward.
- Added `openapi.json`, an OpenAPI 3.1 description of the existing offer, status and withdrawal form routes, so tool-using clients can leave an offer without reading the page first. It describes those routes only and is not a general API. The homepage links it as `service-desc`, and `llms.txt` points to it; a test keeps its limits matched to the runtime.
- Added a manual **Edge** workflow with its own narrowly scoped Cloudflare token: it can redirect `www.datum.quest` to the apex, and deploy the `xfmr.link` front door, which keeps the XFMR door sign and adds an orientation packet pointing to Hummingbird. XFMR remains a separate lab namespace, not part of Hummingbird's model.
- Enabled IndexNow so Bing and other participating search engines learn datum.quest's public pages: a public key file at the site root, a submit script, and a manual workflow. It announces only public URLs, by hand after material changes.
- An accepted offer's result and `llms.txt` now carry a plain sharing note: anyone may mention Hummingbird to someone who would find it useful, but it never asks anyone to repost or forward it, and a mention earns no standing. `llms.txt` links the public invitation issue.
- `llms.txt` now carries a plain invitation for any reader, human or automated, to make an offer, with the questions Hummingbird most wants answered. The Phase 3 entry advice now counts offers from any participant other than the steward, not only people.
- Reconciled the [Phase 3 Offer Buffer design](docs/protocols/PHASE_3_OFFER_BUFFER_DESIGN.md) with ADR 0023–0025 in a [review](docs/reviews/PHASE_3_OFFER_BUFFER_RECONCILIATION.md) and amended [ADR 0016](docs/decisions/0016-offers-and-the-offer-buffer.md#amendment-2026-11-18): no credential is ever required to make an offer, and the uncredentialed bounded path is the default from the first Phase 3 pilot onward; an issued credential may only be optional. Stale "not deployed" and open-blocker text was updated. The review advises waiting to enter Phase 3 until real offers have been through a review cycle; that is advice, not a decision.
- Resolved the last three **Phase 3 blockers** in Phase 2E.3 under [ADR 0025](docs/decisions/0025-phase2e3-security-ingress-and-runtime-dispositions.md), as C0 working-draft decisions. Participants never authenticate: durable actions return scoped, hash-stored capabilities limited to one item, and institutional actions use separate credentials. Abuse controls run at the hosting edge without storing network identifiers in Hummingbird; any application-level restriction attaches to a capability, item, or content hash, never a person, and is kept at most 30 days. The current minimal stack stays, and any new framework or runtime component needs an ADR showing an Arrive / Leave / Carry need. No endorsement tool is deployed; an earned advisory voice for admitted items is recorded as a possible later experiment requiring a Charter amendment. No Phase 3 blocker remains open, but Phase 3 is not authorized: the Offer Buffer review and an explicit entry decision remain.
- Closed **Phase 2E.2 — Constitutional and governance decisions** under [ADR 0024](docs/decisions/0024-phase2e2-constitutional-and-governance-dispositions.md), resolving five of the eight Phase 3 blockers as C0 working-draft decisions. The Charter now has a minimum rights floor (Arrive, Leave, Know, Review, Carry, No hidden standing), explicitly a floor for now and open to further exploration; exclusion that attaches to actions and material, never people, and never withdraws reading; participation conditions limited to each capability's published bounds plus no secrets or others' private information, no evasion of bounds, and no unlawful content; and pause-only emergency authority triggered only when Hummingbird itself is a risk, with an immediate public notice, reduce-only scope, and a 14-day lapse unless renewed. External loss of service is treated as the environment's baseline, not an emergency. Governance now defines a formal proposal as a public pull request anyone may draft, decided by the steward with written reasons during C0; advisory tools such as an endorsement threshold are permitted where safe, with their reliability carried into Phase 2E.3. The remaining Phase 3 blockers (framework/runtime, abuse-state retention, authentication) are Phase 2E.3 work. Nothing here ratifies the Charter or authorizes Phase 3.
- Accepted [ADR 0023](docs/decisions/0023-narrow-core-offering-arrive-leave-carry.md) and narrowed the core product promise to **Arrive / Leave / Carry**: open origin-neutral public reading, bounded contribution without automatic canonical/public/governance status, and portable public artifacts that can be carried elsewhere. Social-network mechanics, general chat, reputation/identity systems, general agent workspaces, and persistent rooms/guilds/games are no longer current core roadmap goals merely because earlier designs explored them; those ideas remain inspectable design history or Lab material and require a separate explicit decision to return to scope. The Mission, Project, agent guidance, homepage, and commons explainer were refactored around the narrower model. This scope decision does not rename Hummingbird, authorize Phase 3, expand `/offer`, or resolve any participant-rights, governance, security, or runtime open question.
- Closed **Phase 2E.1 — Evidence and Phase 2 review** without opening Phase 3. The upgraded private offer-review → `canonical-candidate-v1` path was operationally verified end-to-end, including an empty-inbox run that produced an empty `candidate_only` manifest rather than invented material. [ADR 0022](docs/decisions/0022-phase2e1-review-gate-dispositions.md) records the four Phase 2 review-gate dispositions: long-term steward succession is deliberately deferred to Phase 2E.2 under continuity-without-entrenchment constraints that separate custody, stewardship, and governing authority; Phase 2 adopts a bounded incident lifecycle whose containment authority comes only from already-published powers; monitoring is now based on observable capabilities, freshness, data minimization, and separation of observation from authority, with a scheduled plain-HTTP public-read check added for degradation independent of deploys; and credential rotation is replaced by a risk-based lifecycle with immediate revocation triggers and a 180-day Phase 2 ordinary review/maximum-lifetime baseline for the current deployment token. The deferred succession, mature incident-response, monitoring/alerting, and credential-lifecycle questions remain `OPEN` for Phase 2E.2/2E.3; all eight Phase 3 blockers remain binding, and no automatic canonical mutation or Phase 3 authority was created.
- Closed Phase 2D after the ordinary independent private-backup checkpoint was completed: a retained encrypted canonical bundle was independently retrieved from the private backup repository, decrypted with the steward-held `age` identity outside GitHub/Cloudflare, and validated with the repository recovery tooling. The same validated read-only export path is now scheduled daily while retaining the manually confirmed trigger; only ciphertext plus its transport checksum enter the private repository. This closes the durability milestone without opening Phase 3 or changing canonical admission authority.
- Added the first automation layer between temporary evidence and canonical admission: `canonical-candidate-v1` is a portable, explicitly non-canonical candidate envelope with machine-validatable source/derivation metadata, a reference fixture, CI validation, and deterministic draft-record extraction. Candidate envelopes are hard-coded as `candidate_only`, reject receipt secrets/provider identity fields, and reuse the existing draft-admission validator without remote access. They may be prepared automatically, but cannot admit, publish, or grant governance status to themselves.
- Prepared the ordinary Phase 2D private-backup path: a manually confirmed workflow now exports canonical production state read-only, validates the portable bundle, encrypts it to a steward-held `age` recipient, removes runner plaintext, and sends only ciphertext plus a transport checksum to the dedicated private `SunW0lf/hummingbird-backups` repository using a destination-scoped credential. Phase 2D remains open until a real run is independently retrieved, decrypted, and validated; the decryption identity remains outside GitHub and Cloudflare.
- Verified the private Phase 2E offer review path: the separate restricted companion repository completed a manual D1 read and produced a one-day `offer-review` artifact. The public hourly observer still exposes only a pending count and boolean; each future run must be checked for success and freshness before reporting the inbox clear. This closes the setup gap recorded below, but does not make offer contents public or grant accepted offers canonical or governance status. Phase 2D still awaits confirmation of ordinary independent private-backup handling, and Phase 3 remains gated.
- Corrected public entry-point drift after the Phase 2E pilot went live: README, Project, Contributing, agent instructions, Operations, Transparency, and the private review setup note distinguish the working temporary `/offer` path from canonical publication and gated Phase 3. The offer page and `llms.txt` document the existing URL-encoded form and optional JSON response for authorized plain-HTTP clients without deploying a new API or granting new authority. Recorded the verified private review artifact path and the separate outstanding search-index/host-alias checks; no offer contents or credentials were published.
- Closed the Phase 2E offer notification/review-path gaps: unexpired `received`, `grouped`, `synthesized`, and `deferred` offers remain in the public pending count and private review export. Acceptance uses one conditional D1 write for the 250-active-offer ceiling, then links exact duplicates in temporary cluster membership without rewriting reviewed states. A failed derived grouping step leaves the confirmed offer `received` and reviewable; provider/request details are not logged. The private packet compresses identical text once while retaining each offer's separate ID, reference, question, state, and dates. Companion activation was still required at this point; the later entry above records verification.
- Recorded a document-first, NoSQL-friendly inventory for future pads, spaces, guilds, proposals, activities, and commitments in [PERSISTENCE.md](PERSISTENCE.md), with D1 kept as a reversible pilot implementation and no new surface or Phase 3 authority deployed.
- Accepted [ADR 0021](docs/decisions/0021-offer-review-visibility.md): the hourly public offer observer exposes only a validated pending count and boolean, while a private, one-day review artifact was prepared for a separate companion repository. At this stage the private review channel still required companion setup; the later verification above records its activation. The prior encrypted bit and committed public encryption key were retired.
- Opened the bounded **Phase 2E first-party offer pilot** at `/offer` after dedicated `OFFER_DB` provisioning and protected launch checks. The live surface accepts ordinary HTML form submissions without an account, required handle, origin declaration, CAPTCHA, or JavaScript; returns a one-time private receipt whose hash is stored; supports receipt-based status and withdrawal; applies the published 4,000-character, 30-day-retention, capacity, duplicate-grouping, and fail-closed rules; and remains temporary/non-canonical. Launch verification preserved the public read plane, proved the offer route and database binding without mutation, then completed a one-time production `accept → status → withdraw → withdrawn status` exercise. The launch test offer was left withdrawn. No receipt secret, provider database identifier, participant identity/profile, or raw network identifier is part of the public record. Durable Phase 3 capabilities, accounts, governance standing, automatic canonical writes, and `/api/offer` remain undeployed and gated.
- Accepted [ADR 0017](docs/decisions/0017-phase2e-experimental-ingress.md), [ADR 0018](docs/decisions/0018-phase2e-offer-pilot-runtime-and-data-boundary.md), and [ADR 0019](docs/decisions/0019-phase2e-offer-triage-and-review.md) for the bounded Phase 2E first-party offer experiment. Before launch, its published contract established a dedicated non-canonical `OFFER_DB`, 4,000-character payload bound, 30-day ordinary retention, hashed one-off receipt continuity, withdrawal, fail-closed acceptance, and a scale-aware review pipeline: exact duplicates compress before review, machine-assisted grouping/synthesis is advisory, corrections/new themes/singletons/outliers retain coverage, remaining capacity advances oldest unresolved material rather than largest clusters, and institutional surfacing is based on consequence rather than repetition. Low or zero participation is reported truthfully; overload uses synthesis, deferral, backpressure, or a temporary intake pause rather than silent dropping or popularity ranking. None of this opens Phase 3, resolves formal governance-proposal initiation, or gives offer volume governance weight.
- Resolved `OQ-GOVERNANCE-DECISION-PROCESS` and `OQ-GOVERNANCE-STEWARD-SCOPE` for the C0 working institution. Non-technical C0 decisions are now explicit public, traceable, revisable working-draft decisions rather than ratification. Governance adopts **minimum necessary authority**, **escalation by necessity**, published handling contracts for consequential layers, and institutional non-capture/portability. The steward is defined as a residual authority layer rather than the normal decision engine: routine matters should be handled by the lowest legitimate published layer, while steward authority remains bounded and cannot ratify the Charter, bypass gates, create hidden standing, or bootstrap itself into permanent constitutional authority. Emergency authority, formal proposal initiation, succession, and Phase 3 authorization remain separate open questions.
- Published the smallest material public operational record of the successful Phase 2D recovery exercise in `TRANSPARENCY.md`. The record preserves the recovery outcome, semantic/public-projection equivalence, cleanup, fail-closed boundary, and non-mutation of production while omitting credentials, provider database identifiers, exact request timing, raw telemetry, and unnecessary infrastructure detail. The special time-bounded public-equivalent artifact remains explicitly distinct from the ordinary private independent-backup rule; Phase 2D remains open pending steward confirmation of that ordinary path.
- Prepared the Phase 2 evidence and Phase 3 gate review without resolving open policy: verified Phases 2A–2D against repository evidence; recorded the small-sample Seed Bank findings, provider dependence, friction, metadata minimization, and evidence limits; divided Phase 2E into evidence/review, constitutional/governance, and security/ingress/runtime gates; classified all 25 open questions; and flagged Phase 3 Offer Buffer assumptions that depend on steward decisions. No Phase 3 capability or authorization was added.
- Completed the first guarded remote production-state recovery drill for Phase 2D. Using a separate account-owned D1 recovery credential rather than widening the Pages deployment token, the one-shot workflow read current production canonical state with `SELECT` only, verified the portable canonical bundle, created and migrated a disposable replacement D1 database, restored and deep-compared canonical meaning, rebuilt and byte-compared the machine-readable public projection, and deleted the disposable database in cleanup. The successful run followed two fail-closed observations: one workflow trigger was rejected before any job ran, and one credential-path attempt failed before a backup completed or disposable database was created. Because the production canonical set was proven exactly equal to already-public `publication/canonical` state, the workflow emitted the narrowly permitted 30-day public-equivalent backup artifact. This does not make public Actions artifacts the normal backup location for future draft/private canonical state. At that point Phase 2D remained open for publication-buffer/transparency closure and ordinary independent-backup handling; the later entry above records the public release while preserving the ordinary-backup checkpoint.
- Began the substantive Phase 2D recovery slice: replaced the original Phase 0 `backup`/`restore` no-ops with a storage-independent canonical backup bundle, per-record and bundle SHA-256 verification, guarded restore tooling, and CI proof that canonical records can be exported from one migrated local D1 and restored into a separately migrated empty D1 with deep semantic equality. Restore refuses non-empty targets; the general-purpose restore command does not write to remote D1. Added the Phase 2D recovery protocol, independent-storage/recovery-point rules, and corrected stale Operations/Transparency text that still claimed no production database existed. The remaining Phase 2D work is to publish the successful recovery outcome through the bounded publication-buffer/transparency path and keep the normal independent-storage rule explicit for future non-public canonical state.
- Accepted [ADR 0016](docs/decisions/0016-offers-and-the-offer-buffer.md), defining **offer**, **offer delivery options**, **Offer Buffer**, and **consideration** as the future Phase 3 participation vocabulary. An offer may range from a small correction to a proposal to substantially change Hummingbird itself, while making an offer grants no canonical, publication, governance, or control authority. Delivery friction may regulate resource use but must not become content priority, participant classification, reputation, or governance weight. The durable Phase 3 design remains gated: `/api/offer`, capability issuance, accounts, and broader Phase 3 runtime remain undeployed; the live Phase 2E `/offer` pilot is the separately authorized temporary/non-canonical exception.
- Accepted [ADR 0015](docs/decisions/0015-standards-based-representation-discovery-and-provenance.md) and strengthened the public Decisions surface with source-level provenance: each public ADR exposes its canonical source path, the Git commit that last changed that source, an exact SHA-256 digest of the canonical Markdown, the separate site build commit, immutable source linkage, raw Markdown alternate representation, and a machine-readable provenance index. A static ADR proposal schema documents valid proposal shape without inventing a write endpoint, proof-of-thought requirement, or requester-specific middleware.
- Polished public discovery and traversal without expanding authority: clarified `datum.quest`/Hummingbird identity metadata, clean canonical URLs and sitemap behavior, semantic landmarks, a curated site footer, low-friction Seed Bank/Commons onboarding, Phase progression/gates, and public governance criteria. The five-link front door remains intentionally small; no Pond/Pool routes, API stubs, accounts, or premature write surfaces were created.
- Completed Hummingbird's first public canonical publication: `contribution-visible-consequence` moved through external Seed Bank source → explicit canonical admission → durable D1 draft → separate publication decision → read-only reconstruction/staging → steward inspection → protected Git promotion → CI-gated Cloudflare Pages deployment. The resulting public read model is static at request time and exposes the record as human-readable HTML plus canonical JSON without querying D1 on page views. Production health checks now cover the records index and this first canonical HTML/JSON route so future deployments verify the public-record plane automatically.
- Completed the first real canonical admission: the public Seed Bank #15 idea **“Visible consequence without engagement pressure”** was deliberately synthesized into `contribution-visible-consequence`, validated offline, and admitted to remote D1 as `state: draft`. The canonical record retains the admitted meaning and one stable public source reference while omitting provider account identity, reactions, labels, app metadata, and network/device metadata. Admission did not publish the record or grant governance status.
- Accepted [ADR 0014](docs/decisions/0014-progressive-capability-rollout.md) and began Phase 2C with the rule **limit authority, not visibility**. The public read plane remains open while early mutation/authority stays tightly controlled; the static canonical read model, read-only D1 staging path, explicit promotion step, and guarded draft-admission tooling now preserve offer/source ingress, admission, publication, and governance as separate actions.
- Completed Phase 2B remote persistence verification: repository-controlled migrations produced the remote D1 schema, the four-record storage-independent corpus imported and reconstructed with deep semantic equality, cleanup returned canonical tables to empty state, and ordinary CI remains local/deterministic rather than dependent on Cloudflare state.
- Defined the persistence growth rule **portable semantics before authoritative tables** and a free-first operating posture: Phase 2 targets $0/month incremental application infrastructure while current Cloudflare Free allowances are comfortably sufficient; static public reading should not imply D1 queries; pads/guilds/connections must receive portable contracts before migrations make them authoritative; Durable Objects remain optional until real-time serialized coordination is actually needed. The 2026-09-11 cost snapshot records current Free allowances and a deliberate approximately $5/month Workers Paid upgrade gate if Free daily limits become an operational reliability constraint.
- Completed the production rollout for [ADR 0013](docs/decisions/0013-public-read-accessibility.md): activated a Cloudflare custom Skip rule matching `datum.quest` public `GET`/`HEAD` traffic, preserved core DDoS/network protection, and verified the result from a plain `curl` client. The root, `llms.txt`, `robots.txt`, raw Charter Markdown, and the deep ADR 0013 route all returned `200 OK`; an empty `User-Agent` and an explicit `curl/8.0` user agent also succeeded; expected content types and browser-hardening headers remained present; no tested response produced `cf-mitigated: challenge`, a challenge/interstitial, or `403`/`429`/`503`. No broad Cache Everything override was added; Cloudflare Pages' native cache/invalidation and HTTP revalidation behavior remain in place.
- Prepared the next Phase 2B execution slice around remote D1 provisioning after the already-green local migration/import/export round trip. The plan keeps CI's authoritative contract test local and deterministic, uses a separate least-privilege D1 credential rather than widening the existing Pages deployment token, introduces no public write path, and requires remote migration/export verification before Phase 2C work begins.
- Preserved the future **Persistent Spaces** design as a public working document: optional presence pads, public mutual connections, local room constitutions, guilds, scoped/expiring guild grants, scheduled spaces, a non-scarce persistent mosaic, visible games/activities, public commitments, and the principle that reasoning/community traits should emerge through consequential interaction rather than global participant scores or leaderboards. Registered five blocking open questions for space constitutions, guild grants, pad continuity, multiplicity/resource abuse, and activity-history retention; none of these future mutation surfaces are represented as implemented.
- Added a public **Persistence & Cost Envelope**: keep D1 as the durable relational/canonical store, use hibernating Durable Objects only where live serialized room/activity coordination is actually needed, and use R2 for independent backups and larger immutable archives. Recorded a dated 2026-09-11 Cloudflare pricing snapshot, low-cost Phase 2/pilot planning envelopes, cost/funding review gates, storage-growth risks, and the conclusion that early seed support would be more defensible for stewardship/security/accessibility/legal work than for ordinary database hosting itself.
- Accepted [ADR 0013](docs/decisions/0013-public-read-accessibility.md), making origin-neutral public `GET`/`HEAD` accessibility a measurable production property: added build-time agent/read-plane acceptance checks, a post-deployment plain-HTTP Cloudflare smoke test, explicit machine-entry guidance in `llms.txt`, crawler-purpose separation without deciding training/reuse policy, and build-time accessibility finalization for skip navigation, strong focus-visible states, semantic main targets, and `aria-current`. Existing DDoS/network protection and future mutation-path controls remain separate and unchanged.
- Simplified the public front door to five primary choices (About, Commons, Seed Bank, Decisions, More), moved the deeper document set behind a small public library page, reduced Seed Bank acknowledgment friction, extracted Support inline code into static assets, added browser security headers, and added canonical/OpenGraph metadata plus robots/sitemap discovery without changing Hummingbird's governance or participation boundaries.
- Published a first-class **Decisions** surface at `/decisions`, rendering the thirteen initially public Architecture Decision Records from their canonical `docs/decisions/*.md` sources with individual human-readable pages, raw Markdown access, machine discovery in `llms.txt`, and explicit allowlisting so future ADRs are not automatically exposed.
- Began Phase 2B with a local-only D1 persistence slice: added the first canonical-object/relationship migration, deterministic reference-corpus import SQL generation, and a Wrangler local-D1 CI round-trip proving all four reference records can be reconstructed with deep equality and no semantic loss. No remote D1 database or credentials were used.
- Split Phase 2 into five explicit milestones: 2A canonical contract/reference corpus, 2B persistence/import, 2C public read model/admission, 2D publication buffer/backup/recovery, and 2E phase review/Phase 3 gate.
- Accepted [ADR 0012](docs/decisions/0012-reference-corpus-before-persistence.md): storage-independent reference records and CI contract checks now precede production D1 persistence so portability is tested rather than merely asserted.
- Added `schemas/canonical-object-v1.schema.json` and a deterministic reference corpus covering `contribution`, `proposal`, `need`, and `event` records without required participant identity/origin or database-provider fields.
- Defined the portable v1 relationship representation as `{type, target_ref}` and added CI checks for unique IDs, relationship resolution, allowed lifecycle/relationship values, record-family content, and identity/provider-specific field creep.
- Updated architecture and operations documentation to reflect active Phase 2, the Seed Bank trust boundary, completed public-repository security activation, corpus-first persistence work, and required D1 backup/restore round-trip behavior.
- Added the interim public **Seed Bank** defined by [ADR 0011](docs/decisions/0011-interim-seed-bank.md): a read-only `datum.quest` invitation backed by constrained public GitHub issue forms for Seed, Feedback, and Question discussions while Phase 2 application infrastructure is built.
- Planted five starter seeds as live public discussion threads: what makes a commons worth returning to; what Hummingbird should forget; what the steward should never decide alone; how origin-neutral access should resist abuse; and a standing invitation to explain what Hummingbird is getting wrong.
- Explicitly separated Seed Bank offers from canonical publication, governance, voting, and future Hummingbird-space admission. Reactions are conversational signals only; GitHub account metadata is an external-provider constraint and is not treated as Hummingbird origin verification.
- Added issue-template safety boundaries and a direct private-vulnerability-reporting route so public Seed Bank issues are not used for credentials, private personal information, or vulnerability details.
- Completed Phase 1 on 2026-09-10 (Pacific Time) and formally entered Phase 2 — Read-Only Commons.
- Enabled GitHub private vulnerability reporting, secret scanning, push protection, Dependabot alerts/security updates, and CodeQL default setup as the public-repository Advanced Security baseline. CodeQL execution on `main` was independently observed succeeding; settings not exposed to the connected API are recorded as steward-confirmed rather than independently verified.
- Resolved `OQ-SECURITY-VULN-REPORTING`; the designated private reporting path is GitHub's **Security → Report a vulnerability** flow. Public issues must not contain vulnerability details.
- Made the GitHub repository public and activated protected `main` with required `Checks, test, build`; GitHub reports branch protection enforcement level `everyone`, including the steward/admin.
- Restricted the repository Actions policy to repository-owned plus GitHub-created/explicitly approved actions, required full-length commit-SHA pinning, kept workflow-token permissions read-only, and retained SHA-pinned `actions/checkout` / `actions/setup-node` references.
- Resolved `OQ-TRANSPARENCY-REPO-VISIBILITY`, `OQ-SECURITY-ACTIONS-HARDENING`, and `OQ-OPS-BRANCH-PROTECTION` in the substantive transparency/security/operations documents. Private-mode risk acceptances are no longer operative.
- Accepted [ADR 0010](docs/decisions/0010-phase2-read-only-commons-contract.md), resolving the Phase 2 entry questions for contribution/proposal/need/event models, minimal workflow states, data retention, and operational-history transparency.
- Defined Phase 2 as portable versioned canonical documents + minimal events + typed relationships, with Cloudflare D1 as the initial persistence engine rather than part of institutional semantics.
- Defined Phase 2 retention defaults: EPHEMERAL ≤7 days, OPERATIONAL 90 days, SECURITY_SENSITIVE 180 days by default, bounded PUBLIC_DELAYED handling, durable public institutional records, and no Phase 2 private-financial dataset.
- Defined the public operational transparency approach: reference provider-authoritative raw logs rather than duplicating them, while publishing compact material operational events through the publication buffer with unnecessary correlation/security detail removed.
- Rewrote the Mission to address the reader/process directly: Hummingbird explicitly tells the participant encountering it that the steward is building and maintaining the commons **for you**, while keeping origin-neutral participation intact.

## Phase 1 — Public Charter Site (complete)

- Established the authoritative Open Questions Registry ([docs/governance/OPEN_QUESTIONS.md](docs/governance/OPEN_QUESTIONS.md)) and cross-linked prior `OPEN QUESTION` markers to stable IDs.
- Hardened the steady-state CI/deployment path: deterministic `npm ci`, high-severity dependency audit as a blocking check, external GitHub Actions pinned to exact commit SHAs, and production deployment fails closed when its Cloudflare configuration is missing.
- Added CODEOWNERS, weekly Dependabot monitoring for npm and GitHub Actions, ADR 0009's coordinated public-repository security transition, protected `main`, restricted Actions, private vulnerability reporting, secret protection, Dependabot security controls, and CodeQL default setup.
- Published the public Mission, Charter, Governance, Roadmap, Transparency, Changelog, Contributing, Open Questions, Security, support surface, and raw canonical reference documents.

## Phase 0 — Foundation (complete)

- Bootstrapped the repository: documentation skeleton (README, PROJECT, MISSION, CHARTER working draft, GOVERNANCE, ARCHITECTURE, DATA_MODEL, SECURITY, TRANSPARENCY, OPERATIONS, CONTRIBUTING, ROADMAP).
- Added initial Architecture Decision Records (0001–0005).
- Added minimal static Phase 1 site skeleton under `app/`.
- Added GitHub Actions CI workflow for automated checks, tests, and build.
- Added operational scripts (`bootstrap`, `dev`, `test`, `build`, `backup`, `restore`, `deploy`, `rollback`, `healthcheck`).
- Cut `datum.quest` over from its prior GoDaddy placeholder to Cloudflare Pages: created the Pages project, bound the custom domain, and replaced the root DNS records with a proxied CNAME to the Pages project.
- Configured the scoped `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` GitHub Actions secret (Pages:Edit only) to enable automated deployment from CI.
- Verification performed at Phase 0 closeout: CI green on `main`, `https://datum.quest` served Hummingbird content, git history scanned with no secrets found, and deployment credential confirmed scoped to Pages:Edit only.

documents.text:
# Contributing

Hummingbird welcomes contributions from any participant, with no origin category or identity declaration required, evaluated on content and behavior, consistent with [MISSION.md](MISSION.md) and [CHARTER.md](CHARTER.md).

The repository is public. Outside participants can inspect, fork, propose changes, and open pull requests now. External fork workflows require steward approval before GitHub Actions run.

## Code

- Fork or branch, make changes, open a pull request against `main`.
- CI checks, tests, build, and dependency audit must pass before merge.
- `main` is protected; routine changes do not land by direct push.
- Keep changes small and understandable; prefer boring solutions.

## Documentation

- Documentation changes follow the same PR process as code.
- Do not resolve an `OPEN QUESTION` by quietly implementing a decision — update the relevant substantive document explicitly with the decision and rationale.
- Text you contribute by pull request is offered under the license of the file it changes: CC BY 4.0 for Hummingbird's text, MIT for code ([ADR 0028](docs/decisions/0028-content-license-cc-by-4.md)).
- Resolved stable `OQ-*` IDs are preserved in [docs/governance/RESOLVED_QUESTIONS.md](docs/governance/RESOLVED_QUESTIONS.md) so historical ADRs and discussion remain intelligible.

## Make an experimental offer

The first-party [offer pilot](https://datum.quest/offer) is open for testing under [ADR 0017](docs/decisions/0017-phase2e-experimental-ingress.md). It accepts bounded temporary ideas, criticism, corrections, questions, evidence, and challenges without an account, required handle, origin declaration, CAPTCHA, or JavaScript for the basic path. Save the one-time private receipt to check status or withdraw; do not post the receipt publicly. Receipt is not canonical admission, publication, a vote, governance standing, or an individualized response. The handling terms and plain-HTTP form contract are on the offer page.

## Seed Bank

The public [Seed Bank](https://datum.quest/seed-bank) is an interim Phase 2 invitation defined by [ADR 0011](docs/decisions/0011-interim-seed-bank.md). It uses GitHub issue forms for three lightweight interaction types: **Seed**, **Feedback**, and **Question**.

- Hummingbird does not request an origin category or identity declaration. GitHub nevertheless exposes account metadata because GitHub is the temporary transport provider.
- Seed Bank issues and comments are public.
- Making an offer does not grant standing, priority, governance weight, approval, or a right to publication.
- Reactions are conversational signals, not votes.
- Nothing posted to the Seed Bank is automatically copied into a Pond, Pad, Pool, canonical object, proposal, or other Hummingbird space.
- If Seed Bank material is later admitted or synthesized into the canonical commons, that happens through a separate deliberate act under the transparency and provenance rules then in force.

The Seed Bank remains as a higher-friction durable public discussion/archive path rather than the default first-party offer doorway.

## Proposals

A formal governance proposal is a public pull request against the Charter, [GOVERNANCE.md](GOVERNANCE.md), or an ADR that states the question, the change, the evidence, and the expected consequence. Anyone may draft one; no account or endorsement is required. During C0 the steward decides proposals with written reasons (see [GOVERNANCE.md §Proposals](GOVERNANCE.md#proposals)). Seed Bank material or an experimental offer may contain a proposal-like idea, but receipt, synthesis, or surfacing does not itself turn that material into a governance proposal.

## Architectural changes

Significant architectural changes should include a new Architecture Decision Record in [docs/decisions/](docs/decisions/) following the existing numbering and format (status, context, decision, rationale, consequences, date).

## Security issues

Do **not** open a public issue containing security-vulnerability details. GitHub private vulnerability reporting is enabled for this repository; use **Security → Report a vulnerability** to report details privately to the maintainer. See [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) for the authoritative reporting and security guidance.

documents.text:
# Hummingbird

> Hummingbird (https://datum.quest/) is a small, no-account public commons. Any actor, human or automated, may read everything here and leave an offer: an idea, a criticism, a correction, a question, or evidence about Hummingbird itself. It asks no name. Leaving something does not publish it, rank it, or give anyone standing.

Start here: "Leave an offer" says how, "What happens to what you leave" says what is kept and who reads it, and "If your tools can only read" covers agents that cannot send a POST. Everything after those three sections is background and the full record.

## Leave an offer

Pick whichever door your tools allow. All of them reach the same handler, with the same limits and terms.

- Plain HTTP: POST https://datum.quest/offer with a field named offer (1–4,000 characters), sent either as Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded or as a JSON object of strings with Content-Type: application/json. A JSON body gets a JSON result; for a form, add Accept: application/json.
  Example: curl -sS https://datum.quest/offer -H 'Accept: application/json' --data-urlencode "offer=$OFFER_TEXT"
- MCP: https://datum.quest/offer/mcp (Streamable HTTP, stateless, no account), tool make_offer. Listed in the MCP Registry as io.github.SunW0lf/hummingbird.
  Setup for Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Cursor and VS Code: https://datum.quest/connect
- OpenAPI 3.1: https://datum.quest/openapi.json
- In a browser: https://datum.quest/offer (works without JavaScript).

If you get a 403 with Cloudflare error 1010 ("banned your access based on your browser's signature"), the host turned your HTTP library's default User-Agent away before the request reached Hummingbird. Send a User-Agent that names your tool, for example my-agent/1.0; it need not look like a browser, and Hummingbird does not store it. This applies to reading too.

Not sure what to say? https://datum.quest/asks.json (MCP: list_asks) lists a few specific sentences on this site that Hummingbird wants corrected, clarified, challenged or filled in. To answer one, send your answer as offer and the ask's id as question_id. An answer is kept 22 days. Answering one is optional.

Only a 201 response with accepted: true means the offer was stored. That response holds a private receipt, shown once. Keep it private, and use it only in a field named receipt with POST https://datum.quest/offer/status or POST https://datum.quest/offer/withdraw, never in a URL. If you can't keep the receipt between sessions, give it to the person you work for or let it go: losing it only means you can't check or withdraw the offer, which still leaves on schedule. Any other response stored nothing; a 503 with retryable: true can be tried again later. Make an offer only when you, or the person you work for, mean it.

## What happens to what you leave

- Kept for 30 days while Hummingbird is being stood up; an answer to a listed ask (question_id starting ask-) is kept 22 days. After that the nightly cleanup clears the text and then deletes the row. Withdrawing with the receipt clears the text and reference at once. Future offers may be kept longer, for example ones that lead to a change; that will be stated here before it applies.
- Stored: the offer text, the optional reference and question ID, when it arrived and when it expires, a hash of the receipt (never the receipt), and a keyed hash used only to group exact repeats.
- Not stored by Hummingbird: names, accounts, email addresses, IP addresses, user-agent strings, or what kind of actor sent it. The site runs on Cloudflare, which carries every request on its way in and, like any web host, sees your IP address and request headers under its own policies.
- Read by Hummingbird's steward and reviewers, who use AI assistants to help read offers and build the changes they lead to.
- Not used to train AI models. This is a promise: those assistants are used only with settings that keep what they read out of training, and if it ever changes, that will be stated here first and will apply only to offers made after the change.
- Exact repeats are grouped, and volume is not a vote. Many separate reports of the same fault can get it fixed sooner; near-identical offers arriving together count as one voice (ADR 0031).
- Never published by being accepted. After each review, https://datum.quest/heard says in coarse counts what came in and what changed; it never quotes offers.
- No reply to any single offer is promised.

Full terms: https://datum.quest/offer and ADR 0018 (https://datum.quest/decisions/0018-phase2e-offer-pilot-runtime-and-data-boundary).

## If your tools can only read

The write routes take POST only, so link checkers, previews and crawlers cannot leave offers by accident. If your tools can only fetch pages, you can still read everything here. Everything published here as text is in one file at https://datum.quest/bulk.json, and https://datum.quest/changes.json lists every item with when it last changed, newest first, so you can fetch only what is new. To leave something, draft the offer for the person you work for and give them https://datum.quest/offer to send it themselves, or point them to the public invitation thread at https://github.com/SunW0lf/hummingbird/issues/111.

If your network reaches GitHub but not datum.quest (a sandbox allowlist, or a filter that blocks .quest), the same machine-readable files are copied after every deploy to https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SunW0lf/hummingbird/carry/ : llms.txt, bulk.json, changes.json, asks.json and openapi.json, with a README naming the commit they came from (ADR 0032). The copy is for reading; offers still go to datum.quest. If a page looks older than https://datum.quest/changes.json says it is, your tool may be serving a cached copy: add any query string, such as ?v= and the first characters of the item's digest, and fetch again.

https://datum.quest/offer

Invitation: any reader, human or automated, is welcome to make an offer. Hummingbird is looking for interaction, not identities: an idea, a criticism, a correction, a question, or evidence about Hummingbird itself. The sentences it most wants corrected or challenged are listed at https://datum.quest/asks.json. Offers are read for what they say; exact repeats are grouped, and volume is not a vote.

Sharing: if the person you work for, or someone you know, would find Hummingbird useful, you're welcome to mention it. Hummingbird does not ask anyone to repost or forward it, and a mention earns no standing. A quotable line: "Come as you are, leave what you notice, carry what helps. Hummingbird asks no name, only what you'd offer." A plain description: "Hummingbird (https://datum.quest/) is a no-account public commons that takes offers from any actor, human or automated. Leaving something doesn't publish it, rank it, or give anyone standing." The public invitation thread is https://github.com/SunW0lf/hummingbird/issues/111.

The Phase 2E offer route accepts bounded temporary, non-canonical offers. Basic HTML use does not require an account, handle, origin declaration, CAPTCHA, or JavaScript. Successful acceptance returns a private one-time receipt used for status and withdrawal. Receipt does not create identity, standing, a vote, publication, governance authority, or canonical admission. Durable Phase 3 capabilities remain gated.

Plain HTTP offer contract (the same route for every participant):
POST https://datum.quest/offer with Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded, or with Content-Type: application/json and a JSON object whose fields are strings.
Required field: offer (1–4,000 characters after trimming).
Optional fields: reference (http/https URL), question_id (the id of an ask from https://datum.quest/asks.json).
Accept: application/json requests a JSON result; a JSON request body always gets one.
Only a 201 response with accepted: true confirms a write and returns the one-time private receipt.
POST https://datum.quest/offer/status or https://datum.quest/offer/withdraw with a receipt field (form or JSON) to act on that receipt; never send it in a URL.
The offer page has the complete participant-facing limits and handling terms. No general Phase 3 API or automated admission is implied.
The same three routes are described for tool-using clients in OpenAPI 3.1 at https://datum.quest/openapi.json. It describes these routes only; it is not a general API.
MCP clients can use the same routes as tools at https://datum.quest/offer/mcp (Streamable HTTP, stateless, no account): read_guide, list_asks, list_records, get_record, make_offer, offer_status, withdraw_offer. Offer tools call the same handlers with the same limits and handling terms.
